Coverage against the current website

This preview demonstrates the current design baseline. Geometry and component treatments can evolve together; the branding reference does not fix page layouts. It does not yet cover every production page or interaction. The website currently includes a paginated technical blog, tag-filtered archive, consultation offer and English and Polish articles.

Specimens and remaining gaps
PatternCoverage
Brand, tokens and generic controlsDemonstrated below
Article bodyBasic prose, lists, code and table; TOC, highlighted code and footer still need specimens
Blog index and paginationRequirements documented; dedicated specimens missing
Archive filtering and searchRequirements documented; selected tags, query results and overlay behavior missing
Consultations and bookingThe local demo form is not the involve.me booking flow; full learning-path and provider specimens missing
Conference resourcesDownload, PDF and Tally feedback-wrapper specimens missing
About, Uses and 404Page requirements documented; dedicated layouts missing

See the design documentation review and the page-family requirements in DESIGN.md. Brand references supply the palette and updated logo; page composition is designed for the website.

07 / Content

Room for longer reading

Example article

The problem before the tool

Michał Mazur · 26 September 2026 · 4 min read

Changing a tool can be part of the solution. Start with the process and the decision that needs to be made. A short conversation can establish the scope.

Start with the problem and the constraints before choosing an implementation.

Before the conversation

  • A description of the problem and its effects.
  • An example from everyday work.

Working through the problem

  1. Define the expected outcome.
  2. Compare the available approaches.
  3. Test the selected approach.
Context
The conditions in which the problem occurs.
Constraint
A resource or requirement that affects the choice.
const problem = "Repetitive work";
const result = simplify(problem);
console.log(result);
